messages:
omar: Quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC — hitting a weird interaction between lease revocation and our fallback quotas. Observed pattern: tenant flagged by abuse detector, lease revoked, client immediately reissues requests and gets a new lease from another pool -> thrash and spikes in evictions.
jen: Ugh. Is the new lease coming from the same quota bank or a different shard? :thinking:
omar: Different shard. Eviction doesn't immediately propagate to all schedulers; new admission checks only look at local tokens. We need a stronger handoff so revocation is globally respected, or a soft-quarantine window.
lee: Two quick options: 1) make revocation write a short-lived global tombstone (cheap KV) that admission checks consult, or 2) attach a revocation token/nonce to the client that we validate on new leases.
maria: Tombstone approach seems simpler for immediate consistency, but it adds read on hot path. Nonce/token requires client cooperation and makes client logic more complex (and we can't trust clients if they're abusive).
jen: For tombstones we'd need TTL tuning. Too long and we punish legitimate clients; too short and we still get thrash. What about a hybrid: tombstone with short TTL + local short soft-quarantine (deny new fast-path leases for Xs) so we avoid KV lookups for normal flow.
lee: Sounds good. Also consider tying tombstone writes to sequence numbers so we don't race double-revokes. Example: `revoke_id = {tenant}:{seq}` and admission consults highest seen `revoke_seq`.
omar: Tradeoffs: tombstone reads cost (reads per admission). We can cache tombstone presence in edge LRU for TTL window to reduce read QPS. Also want metrics: revocation -> new lease rate, tombstone read hit ratio.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Scheduled canary for revocation-cache at 03:00 UTC tomorrow. Rolling 20% edge nodes.
maria: Another failure mode: false-positive revokes. Need a rollback path: allow short self-appeal TTL where a tenant can prove innocence and we expire tombstone early. But that invites abuse if misused.
jen: Could limit appeals to verified accounts and surface a manual ops fast-path. For automated, treat appeals as probation — shrink throughput until re-eval.
lee: Implementation sketch:
```
# admission flow
1) check local token fast-path
2) consult local revocation cache (LRU)
3) if cache miss, async read tombstone KV with short TTL and populate cache
4) if tombstone present -> soft-quarantine or deny
```
Keep async read non-blocking by allowing admission to failover to slower fallback (probation) instead of blocking.
omar: Action items: jen will propose TTL ranges + probation rates; lee will prototype cache + async tombstone fetch; maria will write playbook for appeals + ops rollback. We'll sync in infra sync on Thu.
jen: I'll post a quick micro-RFC with numbers today. :thumbsup:
maria: assigning ops on-call to be ready for manual retracts during canary.
lee: I'll open a small PR for the cache shim and add a histogram for tombstone read latency.
omar: Thanks — sounds like a plan. Keeping it conservative for first rollout to avoid accidental mass-deny.
